name: The non-linear axiom (A)
summary: Two single-qubit states built from angles α, β, θ₁, θ₂ are added together, giving a state of the same shape with angles γ, θ₃ where 2$e^{iθ₃}$cos γ = $e^{iθ₁}$cos α + $e^{iθ₂}$cos β.
description:
The first complete axiomatisation of the universal (pure qubit) ZX-calculus without extra generators, by Jeandel, Perdrix and Vilmart, consists of their Clifford+T axioms plus this single rule (A). The left-hand side joins two branches, parametrised by $(\alpha,\theta_1)$ and $(\beta,\theta_2)$, and the right-hand side is a single branch of the same shape parametrised by $(\gamma,\theta_3)$. The rule holds under the side condition $2e^{i\theta_3}\cos\gamma = e^{i\theta_1}\cos\alpha+e^{i\theta_2}\cos\beta$.

Because of this side condition the rule is *non-linear* in the angles. The authors proved that any complete axiomatisation of the universal ZX-calculus that extends the Clifford+T one needs either a non-linear rule or constants that are not multiples of $\pi/4$: all rules that are linear in their angles with $\pi/4$ constants already follow from the Clifford+T axioms. In later work (A) was superseded by the [Euler-angle rule](../euler-angles/).

The stored instance is checked for $\alpha=\frac\pi3$, $\beta=\frac\pi4$, $\theta_1=\frac\pi2$, $\theta_2=\frac\pi6$, with $\gamma$ and $\theta_3$ computed from the side condition.
conditions: 2$e^{iθ₃}$ cos γ = $e^{iθ₁}$ cos α + $e^{iθ₂}$ cos β.
notes: The build checks one instance satisfying the side condition (the variables are restricted to those values).
